title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up the analytic moduli stack M_{1,1}^an, the moduli of complex elliptic curves, as the quotient of a Teichmüller-type space by SL(2,Z).

The rigid objects are 'Torelli structures' (rigidifications): an isomorphism u: Z^2 -> pi_E = H_1(E,Z), compatible with orientation. Via the period lattice inside the tangent line t_E, write z1 = u(e1) and z2 = u(e2).

On the previous page he computed how such a structure changes under g = (a b; c d) in SL(2,Z):
- Under u -> u∘g one gets z1' = a z1 + c z2 and z2' = b z1 + d z2.
- For the natural left action g·u = u∘g^{-1}, with g^{-1} = (d -b; -c a), the ratio tau = z2/z1 transforms as tau' = (a tau - b)/(-c tau + d).
- This is not the textbook formula.

On this page he resolves the mismatch. The 'naive' coordinate would be Z = z2/z1. Instead he uses its reflection in the imaginary axis:
- z = -conj(z2/z1) = -conj(z2)/conj(z1).
- Then Im z = Im(z2/z1), so z lies in D = upper half-plane exactly when (z1,z2) is a direct (positively oriented) basis; the marginal note says this.
- Also conj(tau') = -(az+b)/(cz+d), so z' = (az+b)/(cz+d): 'victoire, c'est la formule habituelle'.
- If one used tau = z2/z1 itself, one would get a different, non-standard transformation formula.

Theorem: D, endowed with the analytic family E_z = C/(Z·1 + Z·(-conj z)), is a universal covering of M_{1,1}^an, corresponding to the classification of elliptic curves with Torelli rigidification.
- The group of M_{1,1}-automorphisms of D is SL(2,Z) acting by g z = (az+b)/(cz+d).
- This matches the natural left action g·u = u∘g^{-1} on Torelli structures.
- Note that E_z is the complex-conjugate curve of the standard C/(Z + Zz), since conj(Z + Z(-conj z)) = Z + Zz.
- SL(2,Z), not PSL(2,Z), is the group: in the stack sense, -1 acts trivially on D but as -1 on the fibres.

The next page draws corollaries:
- pi_1(M_{1,1}) ≅ SL(2,Z) and M_{1,1} ≅ [D/SL(2,Z)].
- Via the comparison theorems, the mapping class group of the once-pointed torus maps isomorphically onto Aut^+(H_1) = SL(2,Z).
- The analogous statement holds for the outer automorphisms preserving the loop structure of a surface group of type (1,1) (Nielsen).

The purpose is to fix sign and orientation conventions so that the Teichmüller tower / Galois–Teichmüller programme rests on an orientation-correct identification T_{1,1} = SL(2,Z).
errors: No mathematical error. The algebra checks: with g^{-1} acting, conj(tau') = -(az+b)/(cz+d), so z' = (az+b)/(cz+d), and Im(-conj tau) = Im tau.

Minor wording tension: he says the M_{1,1}-automorphisms of D operate 'à droite', yet the formula g z = (az+b)/(cz+d) is a left action, and he immediately matches it with the left action g·u = u∘g^{-1}. This is presumably a slip, or a remark about deck transformations versus torsor conventions.

The family E_z = C/(Z + Z(-conj z)) is anti-holomorphic in z as written; it is holomorphic only after identifying it with the conjugate structure. Grothendieck does not comment on this point, which deserves care if 'famille de courbes analytiques' is meant literally.

ideas.what: Period coordinate z = -conj(z2/z1) attached to a direct (oriented) basis of the period lattice, chosen so that the left action u -> u∘g^{-1} becomes the standard Möbius formula.
ideas.modern_name: Sign and orientation conventions for the period map / upper half-plane uniformization of elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass, Jacobi, Klein); a convention issue discussed in many texts (e.g. Deligne–Rapoport, Hain's lecture notes)

ideas.what: The upper half-plane with its universal family is a universal covering of the analytic moduli stack M_{1,1}; the deck group is SL(2,Z), not PSL(2,Z); M_{1,1} = [D/SL(2,Z)] as moduli of elliptic curves with Torelli/Teichmüller rigidification.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold/stack uniformization of M_{1,1}; Teichmüller space T_{1,1}; orbifold pi_1(M_{1,1}) = SL(2,Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Teichmüller theory; Mumford, Deligne–Rapoport for the stack view; Hain, Oort expositions)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), on the Teichmüller tower and pi_1 of M_{g,n} as mapping class groups, including M_{1,1} and SL(2,Z)

ideas.what: Mapping class group of the once-pointed torus is isomorphic to SL(2,Z), and outer automorphisms of the (1,1) loop group restrict isomorphically to Aut^+(H) (announced here, stated on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group Mod(T^2,pt) ≅ SL(2,Z); Dehn–Nielsen–Baer for genus 1

deep.surprise_reason: The page is careful bookkeeping of sign and orientation conventions, choosing z = -conj(z2/z1) so that the Torelli-structure action matches the standard Möbius formula, followed by a standard theorem: the upper half-plane is the universal cover of the stack M_{1,1} with deck group SL(2,Z). It is consistent with the Esquisse's Teichmüller-tower programme but contains nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The definition of D should read D = {z ∈ C | Im z > 0} (upper half-plane), not 'Re z > 0'; this also follows from Im(-conj tau) = Im tau and the marginal remark about direct bases.
'(z par[?] à l'axe imaginaire)' is presumably '(symétrique de ... par rapport à l'axe imaginaire)': z is the reflection of tau = z2/z1 in the imaginary axis.
The struck-out '∈ D' after -conj(z2)/conj(z1) is consistent with the image.
On the next page, 'Z-module libre de rang 1 [?]' should be rang 2 (H = pi^ab for genus 1).
